title: Introduction to GeoIndexR
text: GeoIndexR modern, modular, extensible R package computing spectral geospatial indices multispectral raster data. Built natively terra, GeoIndexR operates SpatRaster objects file paths preserving georeferencing, projection (CRS), resolution, spatial extents. Beyond standard indices, GeoIndexR features secure custom formula engine (geo_index_custom()) enabling users compute mathematical expression spectral bands custom constants.

text: Compute formulas using geo_index_custom():
code: # Compute a custom ratio custom_ratio <- geo_index_custom(   img,   formula = "(nir - red) / (nir + red)",   bands = c(red = "red", nir = "nir"),   name = "MyCustomNDVI" ) print(custom_ratio) #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 10, 10, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 10, 10  (x, y) #> extent      : 440000, 440100, 5410000, 5410100  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : WGS 84 / UTM zone 31N (EPSG:32631) #> source(s)   : memory #> name        : MyCustomNDVI #> min value   :    -0.531245 #> max value   :     0.922703  # Compute a custom parameterized index custom_veg <- geo_index_custom(   img,   formula = "G * (nir - red) / (nir + C1 * red - C2 * blue + L)",   bands = c(blue = "blue", red = "red", nir = "nir"),   params = list(G = 2.5, C1 = 6.0, C2 = 7.5, L = 1.0),   name = "CustomEVI" ) print(custom_veg) #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 10, 10, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 10, 10  (x, y) #> extent      : 440000, 440100, 5410000, 5410100  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : WGS 84 / UTM zone 31N (EPSG:32631) #> source(s)   : memory #> name        : CustomEVI #> min value   : -0.114944 #> max value   :  1.138812

title: End-to-End Multispectral Image Workflow
text: Satellite images often use sensor-specific band notations (B02, B03, B04, B08 Sentinel-2, B2, B3, B4, B5 Landsat 8/9). GeoIndexR supports sensor presets: image layers use non-standard names, can pass custom named vector:
code: # View pre-configured Sentinel-2 bands band_mapping("sentinel2") #>    coastal       blue      green        red   rededge1   rededge2   rededge3  #>      "B01"      "B02"      "B03"      "B04"      "B05"      "B06"      "B07"  #>        nir       nir2   rededge4 watervapor     cirrus      swir1      swir2  #>      "B08"      "B8A"      "B8A"      "B09"      "B10"      "B11"      "B12"  #>       swir  #>      "B11"  # View pre-configured Landsat 8/9 bands band_mapping("landsat8") #>  coastal     blue    green      red      nir    swir1    swir2      pan  #>     "B1"     "B2"     "B3"     "B4"     "B5"     "B6"     "B7"     "B8"  #>   cirrus thermal1 thermal2  thermal     swir  #>     "B9"    "B10"    "B11"    "B10"     "B6" my_mapping <- c(   blue  = "blue",   green = "green",   red   = "red",   nir   = "nir",   swir  = "swir1" )

title: Vegetation Indices in GeoIndexR
text: Vegetation indices exploit distinct spectral reflectance curve healthy green canopies: strong absorption red chlorophyll band (0.64 - 0.67 um) high scattering/reflectance near-infrared (NIR) plateau (0.85 - 0.88 um). GeoIndexR provides four primary vegetation indices, tailored different canopy densities atmospheric soil conditions: NDVI: Normalized Difference Vegetation Index SAVI: Soil Adjusted Vegetation Index EVI: Enhanced Vegetation Index GNDVI: Green Normalized Difference Vegetation Index

title: Vegetation Indices in GeoIndexR
text: Rouse et al. (1974) formulated normalized ratio: NDVI=NIR−REDNIR+RED\text{NDVI} = \frac{\text{NIR} - \text{RED}}{\text{NIR} + \text{RED}} Theoretical range: [−1,1][-1, 1] Values typically range 0.20.2 0.80.8 photosynthetically active green vegetation.
code: library(GeoIndexR) img <- get_example_data()  ndvi <- geo_index(img, "NDVI") index_summary(ndvi) #>  #> === GeoIndexR Spectral Summary === #>  #>  index     min    max   mean median     sd     q05     q25    q75    q95 na_pct #>   NDVI -0.5312 0.9227 0.2984 0.1108 0.4873 -0.3934 -0.0779 0.8676 0.8994      1 #>  total_cells #>          100

title: Vegetation Indices in GeoIndexR
text: areas sparse intermediate canopy cover (<40%< 40\%), exposed background soil alters red near-infrared reflectance. Huete (1988) introduced soil adjustment factor LL: SAVI=NIR−REDNIR+RED+L×(1+L)\text{SAVI} = \frac{\text{NIR} - \text{RED}}{\text{NIR} + \text{RED} + L} \times (1 + L) L=0.5L = 0.5 standard optimal intermediate vegetation density. L→0L \0 approaches NDVI (dense cover), whereas L=1.0L = 1.0 suitable sparse vegetation. GeoIndexR, LL configurable directly geo_index() calc_savi():
code: savi_standard <- geo_index(img, "SAVI", L = 0.5) savi_sparse   <- geo_index(img, "SAVI", L = 1.0)  index_summary(c(savi_standard, savi_sparse)) #>  #> === GeoIndexR Spectral Summary === #>  #>  index     min    max   mean median     sd     q05     q25    q75    q95 na_pct #>   SAVI -0.0736 0.8633 0.3063 0.0676 0.3819 -0.0638 -0.0241 0.7355 0.8459      1 #>   SAVI -0.0677 0.8417 0.2918 0.0613 0.3617 -0.0520 -0.0185 0.6826 0.8261      1 #>  total_cells #>          100 #>          100

title: Vegetation Indices in GeoIndexR
text: Liu & Huete (1995) designed EVI decouple canopy background signal reduce atmospheric influences blue band feedback: EVI=G×NIR−REDNIR+C1×RED−C2×BLUE+L\text{EVI} = G \times \frac{\text{NIR} - \text{RED}}{\text{NIR} + C_1 \times \text{RED} - C_2 \times \text{BLUE} + L} Default coefficients (standard MODIS/Sentinel-2/Landsat): - G=2.5G = 2.5 (Gain factor) - C1=6.0C_1 = 6.0 (Aerosol coefficient red) - C2=7.5C_2 = 7.5 (Aerosol coefficient blue) - L=1.0L = 1.0 (Canopy background adjustment)
code: evi <- geo_index(img, "EVI") index_summary(evi) #>  #> === GeoIndexR Spectral Summary === #>  #>  index     min    max   mean median     sd     q05     q25    q75    q95 na_pct #>    EVI -0.1149 1.1388 0.3675 0.0735 0.4623 -0.0779 -0.0333 0.8732 1.0481      1 #>  total_cells #>          100

title: Vegetation Indices in GeoIndexR
text: Gitelson et al. (1996) substituted red band green band enhance sensitivity chlorophyll concentrations dense canopies red reflectance becomes saturated: GNDVI=NIR−GREENNIR+GREEN\text{GNDVI} = \frac{\text{NIR} - \text{GREEN}}{\text{NIR} + \text{GREEN}}
code: gndvi <- geo_index(img, "GNDVI") index_summary(gndvi) #>  #> === GeoIndexR Spectral Summary === #>  #>  index     min    max   mean median     sd     q05     q25    q75    q95 na_pct #>  GNDVI -0.7659 0.8489 0.2182  0.231 0.5295 -0.5998 -0.3716 0.7401 0.8222      1 #>  total_cells #>          100

title: Water and Moisture Indices in GeoIndexR
text: Delineating water bodies tracking moisture conditions foundational tasks hydrology, wetland monitoring, irrigation management. GeoIndexR implements three key indices: NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index, McFeeters 1996) MNDWI (Modified Normalized Difference Water Index, Xu 2006) NDMI (Normalized Difference Moisture Index, Gao 1996)

title: Water and Moisture Indices in GeoIndexR
text: McFeeters designed NDWI delineate open water features maximizing green band reflectance minimizing NIR reflectance: NDWI=GREEN−NIRGREEN+NIR\text{NDWI} = \frac{\text{GREEN} - \text{NIR}}{\text{GREEN} + \text{NIR}} Water bodies typically positive NDWI values (NDWI>0\text{NDWI} > 0), terrestrial vegetation dry soil display negative values.
code: library(GeoIndexR) img <- get_example_data()  ndwi <- geo_index(img, "NDWI") index_summary(ndwi) #>  #> === GeoIndexR Spectral Summary === #>  #>  index     min    max    mean median     sd     q05     q25    q75    q95 #>   NDWI -0.8489 0.7659 -0.2182 -0.231 0.5295 -0.8222 -0.7401 0.3716 0.5998 #>  na_pct total_cells #>       1         100

title: Water and Moisture Indices in GeoIndexR
text: urbanized complex landscapes, built-surfaces often produce false positive signals classical NDWI. Xu (2006) replaced NIR band Shortwave Infrared (SWIR) band: MNDWI=GREEN−SWIRGREEN+SWIR\text{MNDWI} = \frac{\text{GREEN} - \text{SWIR}}{\text{GREEN} + \text{SWIR}} built-areas reflect strongly SWIR, MNDWI values negative, clearly separating urban structures open water.
code: mndwi <- geo_index(img, "MNDWI") index_summary(mndwi) #>  #> === GeoIndexR Spectral Summary === #>  #>  index     min    max    mean  median     sd    q05     q25    q75    q95 #>  MNDWI -0.5512 0.8414 -0.0692 -0.3565 0.5143 -0.503 -0.4426 0.5909 0.8118 #>  na_pct total_cells #>       1         100

title: Water and Moisture Indices in GeoIndexR
text: Normalized Difference Moisture Index monitors vegetation liquid water content: NDMI=NIR−SWIRNIR+SWIR\text{NDMI} = \frac{\text{NIR} - \text{SWIR}}{\text{NIR} + \text{SWIR}} Higher values indicate well-hydrated vegetation canopies, whereas low negative values signal drought water stress.
code: ndmi <- geo_index(img, "NDMI") index_summary(ndmi) #>  #> === GeoIndexR Spectral Summary === #>  #>  index     min    max   mean median     sd     q05     q25    q75    q95 na_pct #>   NDMI -0.3558 0.6853 0.2397  0.341 0.3298 -0.2609 -0.1321 0.5173 0.6174      1 #>  total_cells #>          100

title: Computation of Spectral and Geospatial Indices from Multispectral Raster Data
text: 🛰️ Unified SpatRaster & File Path API: Pass terra::SpatRaster objects direct file paths ("image.tif"). 🧩 Custom Formula Engine (geo_index_custom()): Define arbitrary mathematical expressions ("(nir - red) / (nir + red)") custom parameters secure AST execution. 🎯 Intelligent Band Resolution: Map bands index (c(red = 3, nir = 4)), layer name (c(red = "B4", nir = "B8")), sensor preset (sentinel2, landsat8, landsat9). ⚖️ Reflectance & Scale Factor Management: Built-support scale_factor = 10000 convert integer Digital Numbers (DN) physical surface reflectance [0,1][0, 1]. 🛡️ Zero-Division & Singularity Safety: Automatic near-zero denominator tolerance conversion non-finite values NA without arbitrary clamping. 📚 Rich Metadata Registry (index_registry()): Comprehensive catalog indices descriptions, purposes, interpretations, limitations, literature citations. 📊 Descriptive Statistics & Plotting: Detailed summaries percentiles (index_summary()) thematic color ramps (plot_index()).

Compute a standard index ndvi <- geo_index(img, "NDVI", bands = c(red = "red", nir = "nir"))  # 3. Compute a scale-sensitive index with scale_factor (e.g. for Sentinel-2 DN) evi <- geo_index(   img,   "EVI",   bands = c(blue = "blue", red = "red", nir = "nir"),   scale_factor = 1 # or 10000 for raw integer DN )  # 4. Compute a custom user formula custom <- geo_index_custom(   img,   formula = "(nir - swir1) / (nir + swir1)",   bands = c(nir = "nir", swir1 = "swir1"),   name = "CustomMoistureIndex" )  # 5. Summarize statistics with percentiles index_summary(ndvi)  # 6. Plot the index plot_index(ndvi, "NDVI")  # 7. Save output to GeoTIFF writeRaster(ndvi, "NDVI_result.tif", overwrite = TRUE)

title: Calculate Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) — calc_ndvi
text: $$NDVI = \frac{NIR - RED}{NIR + RED}$$ Description & Purpose: NDVI widely used remote sensing index monitoring vegetation greenness, photosynthetic activity, canopy vigor. Chlorophyll pigments green leaves absorb red light strongly, spongy mesophyll structure scatters near-infrared light. Direct Band Usage vs geo_index(): geo_index(image, "NDVI") handles multi-band raster extraction band mapping automatically, calc_ndvi() direct, lower-level computation function works : Individual single-layer terra::SpatRaster objects (e.g. nir = img[["nir"]], red = img[["red"]]). Standard R numeric vectors, scalars, matrices. Value Range & Interpretation: 0.6 0.9: Dense, healthy green vegetation (forests, mature crops). 0.2 0.5: Moderate sparse vegetation (grasslands, shrublands, young crops). 0.0 0.1: Bare soil, rock, sand, impervious urban areas. < 0.0: Water bodies, snow, ice, clouds.

title: GeoIndexR 0.1.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-10-10 Initial CRAN-ready release GeoIndexR. Core framework computing spectral indices using terra::SpatRaster. Unified high-level functions: geo_index(), geo_indices(), geo_index_all(). Direct vectorized band calculation functions: calc_ndvi(), calc_savi(), calc_evi(), calc_gndvi(), calc_ndwi(), calc_mndwi(), calc_ndbi(), calc_ndmi(), calc_bsi(). Generic band calculator calc_index(). Centralized metadata catalog via index_registry() list_indices(). Sensor presets Sentinel-2, Landsat-8/9, Landsat-5/7 via band_mapping(). Numerical safety: safe division preventing zero-division crashes silent infinite values. Summary statistics index_summary() thematic visualization plot_index(). Bundled lightweight synthetic dataset example_multispectral. Complete testthat test suite 4 vignettes.
